reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for His people through multiple protective acts: He sends His angel to position Himself between the Egyptian and Israelite camps (וַיִּסַּע מַלְאַךְ הָאֱלֹהִים), provides divine light for Israel and darkness for the Egyptians (וַיְהִי הֶֽעָנָן וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיָּאֶר אֶת־הַלָּיְלָה), fights directly for the Israelites (יְהוָה יִלְחַם לָכֶם), looks down upon the Egyptian camp and defeats them (וַיַּשְׁקֵף יְהוָה אֶל־מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם וַיָּהָם אֵת מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם), and ultimately saves Israel from Egyptian bondage (וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהּוּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל). The passage culminates with the people's faith in Yahweh (וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּֽיהוָה), affirming the efficacy of His protective care.
